Directions for Use
 
 
Handwash: Use two scoops of detergent per 5 to 8 pieces of clothes. Dissolve washing powder fully in water. Soak for 15 to 30 minutes before washing. 
Machine wash: Use three scoops of detergent per 8 to 12 pieces of clothes. 
 
Caution: Keep out of reach of children. If the product comes in contact with eyes, flush with clean water for at least 15 minutes. If swallowed, do not induce vomiting, and consult your doctor. Wear gloves if you have sensitive or damaged skin.
 
Warning: May burn but does not ignite readily. Avoid contact with incompatible substances and excessive heat.
 
Signs and Symptoms of Poisoning
 
 
Ingestion: May cause stomach pain or vomiting. 
Skin Contact: Prolonged contact may cause dryness of the skin. 
Eye Contact: May cause eye irritation. 
 
First Aid
 
 
Inhalation: Move the exposed person to fresh air immediately. If any discomfort continues, contact the poison control center. 
Skin Contact: Rinse the affected area with a large amount of water until no evidence of product remains. Get medical attention if irritation persists. 
Eye Contact: Immediately rinse eyes with plenty of water, occasionally lifting upper and lower lids, until no evidence of product remains. Get medical attention if pain or irritation persists. 
Ingestion: If vomiting occurs, keep the head below the hips to prevent aspiration. Dilution by rinsing the mouth and giving water or milk to drink is generally recommended. If unconscious, the victim should not be given anything to drink and contact the poison control center immediately.
